---
title: "Genotype and structure above the probe"
---

## 21. Genetic variation under the probe

Every section above treats a beta value as a measurement of methylation. It is
also, in part, a measurement of genotype, and the two are not separable by
looking at the number.

### 21.1 A probe sits at a genomic coordinate

Each probe has a chromosome and a base position, so the probe set can be
intersected with any variant catalogue: ClinVar for clinically annotated
variants, dbSNP for the general catalogue. The intersection is an ordinary
range join, which `GenomicRanges` or `bedtools` will do, and it answers a
question that matters before scoring: does this clock depend on probes whose
signal a common variant can move.

### 21.2 Three ways a variant reaches the beta value

**A SNP at the interrogated base.** Single-base extension reads the variant
rather than the methylation state, so the beta becomes a genotype readout. This
is the population of probes the published masks remove, and it is why
FALCONAge applies the Zhou masks rather than treating every probe as equally
informative.

**A SNP under the probe body.** Hybridisation is weakened, intensity falls, and
the beta drifts toward the middle of the range without any obvious signature of
failure.

**Cross-reactivity.** A 50-mer against a three-base genome maps to more than one
locus more often than the design intends. Chen and colleagues catalogued these
for the 450K, and the affected probes carry a mixture of signals from several
places in the genome.

### 21.3 meQTL: the variant is somewhere else entirely

A methylation quantitative trait locus is a variant associated with methylation
at a CpG, usually nearby but sometimes far away. GoDMC and the EPIGEN meQTL
resource map these genome-wide. The consequence for a clock is direct: if a
clock CpG is under strong meQTL control, part of the between-person variance in
that clock is genetic and fixed at conception rather than acquired, and no
intervention will move it.

::: {.callout-note}
## What this changes about a score

A clock's between-person variance splits into an acquired component, which is
what the clock is meant to measure, and a genetic component, which is not. The
split is not visible in the score. Two people with the same clock age can differ
because one has lived differently and the other inherited a different genotype
at a handful of high-weight probes.
:::

### 21.4 The arrays carry genotype probes on purpose

450K and EPIC include rsID-labelled SNP probes, 65 on the 450K, for sample
identity. They confirm that two arrays came from the same person, which is the
check that catches a swapped sample. `MethylToSNP` goes further and infers
genotypes from the methylation pattern itself, which is useful and is also a
reminder that array data is identifiable.

## 22. Structure above the single probe

### 22.1 A clock is a combination score

A clock sums hundreds of weighted features, which makes it the same kind of
object as a polygenic risk score, and methylation risk scores for individual
traits are built the same way. The TranslAGE panel is largely made of them:
1,694 of its 1,803 biomarkers are proxies for proteins, metabolites and clinical
values rather than clocks.

The shared property matters more than the shared arithmetic. A combination score
is robust where a single probe is noisy, and it is opaque in the same measure: a
change in the total does not say which component moved. That is the argument for
the subscore clocks in section 5.

### 22.2 Co-methylation modules

CpGs covary. Weighted correlation network analysis groups them into modules and
summarises each by its first principal component, and the module can then be
tested as one unit rather than as several thousand correlated tests. This is
where the multiple-testing burden of an epigenome-wide scan becomes tractable,
and it recovers structure that a per-probe analysis cannot see.

### 22.3 Allele-specific methylation

The two alleles at a locus can carry different methylation, and the pattern can
follow a haplotype block. Array data cannot resolve this because a beta value
averages both alleles into one number. Sequencing can, and tools such as
MethHaplo combine allele-specific methylation with genotype to identify the
regions involved. Imprinted loci are the familiar case and not the only one.

### 22.4 Interactions between variants are real and small

Genome-wide tests for SNP by SNP effects on methylation find them, and find that
they explain little variance. The practical reading is that additive models are
not leaving much on the table at this level, which is consistent with the
observation in section 4 that elastic net remains competitive with deep networks
on this problem.
